answer.what_it_does: American Express Global Business Travel (Amex GBT) provides business travel management software and services, including booking, servicing, payments, expense, and travel support. Its recent AI work focuses on agentic travel servicing: conversational assistants and orchestration layers that search, book, manage, and resolve travel requests within policy and with escalation to human counselors.[1][4][6]

ai_agents.name: Egencia AI connector in Claude
ai_agents.what_it_does: Enables travelers and enterprise AI agents to search, book, and manage policy-compliant air and hotel travel within Claude, without leaving the enterprise AI environment.[1]
actions: Routes tasks through Amex GBT agentic orchestration layer

ai_agents.name: Amex GBT agent-to-agent orchestration layer
ai_agents.what_it_does: An AI orchestration architecture that interprets traveler requests, breaks them into tasks, and routes each task to specialized agents for end-to-end managed travel workflows.[1]

ai_agents.name: AI chatbot with travel counselor handoff
ai_agents.what_it_does: Provides instant responses to traveler questions and then brings in a travel consultant when additional help is needed.[6]
actions: Hands off to live travel consultants

ai_agents.name: Complete by SAP Concur integrated chat
ai_agents.what_it_does: An enterprise integrated chat experience for travel booking, servicing, payments, and expensing, with automated handoff to a live travel counselor and future SAP Joule support.[8]
actions: Hands off to live travel counselor

ai_agents.name: Hotel Lobby
ai_agents.what_it_does: An agentic AI capability for hotel sourcing that automates data-intensive tasks and shortens procurement cycles.[7]

use_cases.name: Policy-compliant booking in enterprise AI
use_cases.who_uses_it: Travelers and enterprise AI agents using Claude with Amex GBT connectivity.[1]

use_cases.name: Conversational servicing with escalation
use_cases.who_uses_it: Business travelers and travel program users supported by Amex GBT chat services.[6][8]

use_cases.name: Hotel program sourcing and optimization
use_cases.who_uses_it: Hotel program managers and sourcing consultants.[7]

use_cases.name: Travel booking, servicing, payments, and expensing
use_cases.who_uses_it: Corporate travelers and enterprise customers using Complete by SAP Concur and Amex GBT.[8]

incidents_or_risks.what: Amex GBT has highlighted governance and risk as a concern for agents talking to each other, noting that new agent-to-agent dynamics require thoughtful controls around risk profile changes.[9]
Amex GBT said its AI deployments use trusted data, governance, and transparency principles, indicating risk management is part of the design for its broader agent-to-agent architecture.[7]

facts.claim: Amex GBT describes Complete as a booking, servicing, and expensing solution that is flexible, powered by AI, and seamless.[4]
Amex GBT says its AI chatbot works alongside professional travel counselors to answer traveler questions.[3][12]
Amex GBT said its Egencia Chat handled 470,000 conversations in 2024.[11]
Amex GBT said AI can accelerate value creation by improving customer experience, powering agentic transformation of B2B travel, and reducing operating costs.[13]
Amex GBT said its agentic travel assistant can search, book, and manage travel in a single conversation.[14]

answer.what_it_does: American Express Global Business Travel (Amex GBT) utilizes AI-driven agents and automation to streamline travel booking, servicing, and policy compliance for corporate clients. These technologies are integrated into their platforms to provide real-time assistance, automate complex travel management tasks, and improve the overall traveler experience.

ai_agents.name: Amex GBT AI-powered virtual assistant
ai_agents.what_it_does: Provides automated, real-time support to travelers for booking, itinerary management, and travel disruption handling.

facts.claim: Amex GBT integrates AI to scale servicing capabilities and reduce manual intervention in the travel booking lifecycle.

answer.what_it_does: American Express Global Business Travel (Amex GBT) is a travel management company and software provider that has been adding agentic AI to its booking, servicing, and hotel sourcing products. Its newest agent layer, an agent-to-agent architecture, lets travelers and enterprise AI agents search, book, and manage policy-compliant trips from inside outside tools such as Claude and Google Chat.

ai_agents.name: Egencia AI connector in Claude
ai_agents.what_it_does: Lets a traveler or an enterprise AI agent use Claude to review upcoming schedules, propose itineraries, and book air and hotel travel within corporate policy.
actions: Reads the user's calendar to identify upcoming trips (as described for the Claude example)
Searches, books, and manages air and hotel reservations
Applies corporate travel policy rules during booking
Runs on Amex GBT's proprietary agent-to-agent architecture

ai_agents.name: Hotel Lobby
ai_agents.what_it_does: A multi-agent system inside Amex GBT Consulting that automates hotel sourcing work such as data preparation, rate targets, and RFP checks, while consultants keep control of strategy and negotiation.
actions: Draws on negotiated-rate benchmarks across many properties
Uses supplier performance metrics from more than $5 billion in managed hotel spend
Supports continuous, year-round rate and compliance monitoring

ai_agents.name: Egencia LLM virtual agent
ai_agents.what_it_does: A large-language-model chat agent that answers Egencia customer questions and handles routine self-service requests before a traveler needs a human consultant.
actions: Answers account and help questions in ten languages
Handles self-service requests such as password resets and adding a frequent flyer number
Escalates to travel consultants when needed

incidents_or_risks.what: Industry commentary from an Amex GBT executive says agent-to-agent interactions change the travel risk profile, so deployments need governance around them to keep the company's risk level unchanged.

Amex GBT says it invested materially in information security and identity and privileged access management controls to govern its AI ecosystem, and that it applies the same security and privacy standards to AI as to other systems.

Press coverage notes that the agentic travel tools operate in an area governed by policy and contracts, and that the Claude connector's consequential transactions are a test of whether automated booking can be trusted at corporate scale.

facts.claim: Amex GBT launched the Egencia AI connector in Claude on July 27, 2026, described as one of the business travel industry's first agentic booking integrations; early adopters were expected in August 2026 with general availability expected by end of 2026.
The Claude connector is the first deployment of Amex GBT's proprietary agent-to-agent architecture, described as an agentic layer that puts full travel management services inside any AI environment.

Hotel Lobby launched in October 2026 as an agentic AI capability within Amex GBT's hotel sourcing consulting service, and is available worldwide to Amex GBT Consulting clients and enterprise travel programs.
Amex GBT says its agent-to-agent architecture is already live across its travel servicing and booking products, and Hotel Lobby is built on the same governance and transparency principles.

Amex GBT's hotel sourcing methodology is cited by the company as delivering 28.8% average savings off the Best Available Rate and a 96% property response rate across more than 80,000 hotels sourced annually.

In May 2025 Amex GBT launched an LLM-powered virtual agent for Egencia customers and a natural language query feature for Egencia Analytics Studio; in a trial, nearly a third of users who used the virtual agent self-served without waiting for a consultant.
Amex GBT's clients include Citi, Synovus, and other financial institutions, businesses, and government agencies that manage staff travel expenses.
Amex GBT was taken private following a US$6.3bn acquisition by an AI-focused holding company.

Amex GBT-commissioned Forrester research found that 3% of surveyed organizations describe travel as part of a fully orchestrated enterprise workflow, while 92% of IT decision-makers expect AI to make travel continuously optimized.
Amex GBT says it will also deliver machine-learning, LLM, and natural-language chat AI products within Complete by SAP Concur and Amex GBT.
